headline: Silversides Stack Robinson's Hole — First Bonito Flash Off Wasque
subhead: The bait's finally thick enough to hold fish, and the season's first bonito scouts just showed on the Vineyard's south side.
body_markdown:
Silversides are balling up tight in the rip at Robinson's Hole right now, thick enough that you can see the nervous water from fifty yards off before you ever see a bird. Squid are mixed in behind them, working the current seam on the Vineyard side of the hole, and that combination — squid and silversides stacked in a rip that's running hard on this full moon — is exactly what gets me up before the sun this time of year. It's the tell. Bait like that doesn't sit still long before something shows up to eat it.

And something did. First bonito scouts of the season flashed off Wasque this week, working the rip where the south shore current dumps into open water. Not a blitz, not consistent, just single fish and pairs showing on the surface for a few seconds at a time before disappearing back down. We flagged this corridor last week as sitting right on the edge of the turnover, with water warming into that low-to-mid-70s window and bait building — and here's the first confirmation. It's early. I want to be straight about that. One or two fish showing off Wasque is not a green light to run down there expecting a bonito blitz. But it's the signal I watch for every August, and it's right on schedule. I'd expect the next push to come through Menemsha and down into Robinson's Hole within the next week to ten days if this bait holds and the water doesn't get knocked back by a cold northeast blow.

Striped bass are locked into the low-light pattern you'd expect for mid-August — daytime fishing has been tough unless you're working current-swept structure or a river mouth that's holding a few degrees cooler than the open bay. Dawn and dusk around Woods Hole, working the rip off the draw pilings and down through the Eel Pond cut, has been the most dependable window. Bunker pods are scattered through the Elizabeth Islands side, and where you find them tight to structure — Quick's Hole, the lee side of Nashawena — bass are still showing under them at first light. I've had the best luck swimming a 3-ounce white bucktail with a white curly-tail trailer down through the deeper part of the rip on the last of the outgoing, letting it sink to the bottom third before working it back up through the water column slow. Nothing has been easy about it. You put in your dues at 5 a.m. or you don't connect.

Fluke have been the one thing I can send people to with real confidence. Doormats are holding on the channel edges and drop-offs where the bottom breaks from eight feet down into eighteen or twenty — the mouth of Quick's Hole, the edges of the Cuttyhunk channel, and the deeper cuts running out of Vineyard Sound toward Woods Hole. This full moon tide swing has been sharpening the drift bite right at the tide changes, which lines up with what I've been seeing on the water — slow periods, then a tight ten or fifteen minutes where three or four rods go down at once as the current eases through the turn. White Gulp Swimming Mullets on ¾-ounce bucktails, dragged slow right along bottom, have been outfishing everything else I've thrown. Keep a squid strip on the hook if you can — the squid showing up in the rips right now tells you what these fish are already keyed on.

Bluefish are mixed. Snapper blues are thick in the back bays — Menemsha Pond, the shallows off Lambert's Cove — giving light-tackle guys steady, easy action on small metal and Kastmasters. The bigger cocktail blues haven't fully shown yet, but with peanut bunker starting to spread through the bay the way they are, I'd expect that to change fast. We called that pattern out a little over a week ago, and the bait's tracking right where we said it would. Give it another week and I think the cocktail blues push into the same rips holding the fluke and bass, especially around the Cuttyhunk side where the peanuts are thickest right now.

Scup remain the honest, boring-but-reliable fishery — Woods Hole structure, the Cuttyhunk breakwater, and the pilings around Menemsha basin are still stacked with them on squid strips and sandworms, bottom-fished on light tackle over rocky patches in ten to twenty feet. Good for a box of dinner fish while you wait on the tide to turn for something bigger.

Looking ahead, the moon coming off full should ease the current strength a touch by midweek, which usually settles the bite windows back into a more normal rhythm rather than the exaggerated swings we've had. I'll be watching Robinson's Hole and the Wasque rip closely — if that bait holds and water stays in the mid-70s, I expect the bonito reports to firm up fast, with albies not far behind. That's the pattern every year on this water. The first flash is never the run. But it's never wrong either.
